summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including mitochondrial disease, autonomic neuropathy with POTS, coronary artery disease, pacemaker, polycystic kidney disease, and recent TURP surgery was admitted for presyncope, malaise, and transient visual changes. He had poor oral intake and symptoms of prostate pain and dysuria post-operatively, though urine culture was negative. Workup revealed no cardiac ischemia, normal head imaging, and improvement in renal function with IV fluids. His presyncope was attributed to hypovolemia, and neurology deemed his visual episodes consistent with prior TIAs without need for acute intervention. Prostate pain was managed symptomatically. He improved with supportive care and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for neurologic evaluation.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Disorder of the autonomic nervous system, unspecified
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
Encounter for adjustment and management of other part of cardiac pacemaker
